name: Bimatoprost

lead: Bimatoprost is a synthetic prostaglandin F2-alpha analogue approved in 2001 as eye drops for glaucoma and ocular hypertension. In 2008 it received FDA approval as Latisse for eyelash hypotrichosis, after patients using the drops noticed longer, darker lashes.
In appearance communities it is used for lash enhancement and, off-label, for eyebrows. Randomised trials show increases in lash length, thickness and darkness, with effects that fade after stopping.

paras: Bimatoprost is thought to prolong the anagen growth phase of eyelash follicles and to increase the number of follicles in the growth phase, and may stimulate melanogenesis, which darkens lashes. It acts on prostaglandin-related receptors in the follicle.

Common effects are eye redness, itching and eyelid skin darkening, and it can cause permanent darkening of the iris, particularly in hazel or mixed-colour eyes, and periorbital fat atrophy that gives a sunken look. It is prescription-only and should be applied carefully at the lash line; use near the eye carries irritation risks. Lashes return to baseline after discontinuation.
